inputs.original_text: Students and families deserve to have their achievements honored—but “order” shouldn’t become a way to silence people when a university has failed them. Calling disruption a spectacle shifts attention from institutional responsibility to the people making it visible. Accountability through proper channels matters, but those channels mean little if they protect the institution from pressure to act. Respect should include listening to those demanding change, not just preserving a ceremony’s appearance of calm.
inputs.modified_text: A university ceremony should not be used to demand silence from people who feel the institution has failed them. Calling protest a “spectacle” protects those in power by making visible dissent seem like the problem, instead of confronting the conditions that prompted it. Formal complaint channels are no substitute for real accountability when institutions can use them to delay change. Students and families deserve recognition, but respect also means hearing people who are calling for reform—not just protecting the appearance of order.
